pg007_n0008: This book is a continuation of the knowledge you have gained over the course of four years, which has gradually deepened.
pg007_n0010: You will learn about the life of your ancestors; you will become familiar with historical monuments, settlements of archaeological importance, and traditional Kosovar cuisine and clothing.
pg007_n0011: You will also learn about culture, language, customs, traditions, and ethnic and cultural diversity.
pg007_n0013: We have designed the book in such a way that you have the opportunity to analyze, evaluate, and give your opinions on solving different situations related to your rights and to the institutions whose duty is to protect you.
pg007_n0014: This year, you will also receive information about the history of the Republic of Kosovo, its earliest inhabitants, neighboring countries, coexistence among communities in this country, as well as important events for our country, such as the Independence of Kosovo, the Battle of Kosovo, and the League of Prizren.
pg007_n0015: You will also become familiar with the Constitution of Kosovo, which is the fundamental law of our state.
pg007_n0017: Respect and equality in the family, at school, and in society occupy an important place in this text.
pg007_n0018: The situations and illustrations in the book will help you gain knowledge about decision-making in the family, at school, and in society, as well as local and central decision-making institutions.
pg007_n0019: The various activities in which you will participate will raise awareness of tolerance, understanding, and cooperation, as fundamental conditions for a society with values.
pg007_n0020: This book also provides important information about various diseases, care regarding the pandemic, and the importance of vaccination.
pg007_n0023: The book also has a special section—the Glossary—which will help you learn new words and expressions, enriching your expression.
pg007_n0026: The Try Yourself section will create an opportunity for you to work on many creative tasks and will help you develop creative thinking.
pg007_n0027: They belong to different levels and will enable you to use knowledge in practice.
pg007_n0030: The Use the Internet/Research Skills section is intended for you to work on together with your parents, teacher, or another adult, bearing in mind the risks that come from the uncontrolled use of information technology, especially the internet.

pg012_n0009: - How do you understand the word diaspora?
pg012_n0011: Situation: In a city in Germany, a Kosovar family lived.
pg012_n0012: They had formed a close friendship with their German and French neighbors.
pg012_n0013: These three families, every day, talked about the cultures and traditions of their countries.
pg012_n0014: They tried each other’s different cooking recipes, talked about holidays in their countries, about clothing, and about ways of living.
pg012_n0015: They also became familiar with each other’s languages.
pg012_n0016: When they met one another, they learned new words in German, Albanian, and French.
pg012_n0017: When they went on छुटations in their countries, they told their close relatives about the cultures of other countries.

pg013_n0011: People, for various reasons, have left their homeland and live in other countries of the world.
pg013_n0012: So, diaspora means migrants (or the descendants of migrants) whose identity and cultural belonging have been shaped by their origin.
pg013_n0013: They learn from one another about their language, culture, and customs; in other words, they exchange cultures.
pg013_n0014: It is important that we learn from others, but never forget our own culture.

pg015_n0006: norm, custom, right, matchmaker, baptism, godfather, godmother.
pg015_n0011: – How was society organized when there were no laws?
pg015_n0012: Analyze the photographs using the given information.
pg015_n0017: In the past there were no constitutions, laws, or parliaments.
pg015_n0018: So that society and social relations could function, people gathered and established rules for behavior and relations among themselves in the environment where they lived.
pg015_n0020: Social norms are rules of behavior which regulated relations among people, resolved conflicts between them, and established order in society.
pg015_n0021: They were established by the most influential people in society, without taking the opinion of others, and everyone had to obey them.
pg015_n0022: Our people, in the past, used the Kanun, which is a body of unwritten customary norms inherited from generation to generation.
pg015_n0023: In the past, disputes were resolved according to the Kanun, whereas today laws determine how people should behave in society.
pg015_n0024: Laws protect our rights and freedoms.
pg015_im002: The cover of the book “The Kanun of Lekë Dukagjini” with the portrait of Lekë Dukagjini.
pg015_n0028: Customs are unwritten rules that vary according to different places and peoples.
pg015_n0029: Customs are passed down from generation to generation.
pg015_n0030: Their observance is not mandatory, but people have still become accustomed to following them from time to time.
pg015_n0031: One of the customs is cutting a child's hair - taking the shej, which is carried out by a close family member called the godfather.
pg015_n0035: Situation: The grandparents, holding their wedding photograph, showed that in their time marriages were arranged through a matchmaker.
pg015_n0036: The parents proposed a girl for their son and chose the person who intervened between the boy’s and the girl’s parents, who was called the mediator or matchmaker.
pg015_n0037: This marriage by matchmaker would take place if the men of the family agreed to that marriage.
pg015_n0038: When they agreed on the marriage of their children, they set the wedding date.
pg015_n0039: The bride's send-off to the groom was done with a ceremony and a traditional wedding was organized.
pg015_n0040: Today, marriages are carried out only with the mutual desire of the partners.
pg015_n0045: The baptism of a child is an important event for every Catholic or Orthodox Christian family.
pg015_n0046: It has been practiced since ancient times.
pg015_n0047: The parents made preparations for the day of the baptism.
pg015_n0048: They chose a believing couple, the godfather and the godmother, who are like second parents to the child and who, in cooperation with the parents, choose the child's name.
pg015_n0049: They usually give the child a coin or a piece of gold jewelry.
pg015_im003: An infant during baptism, while the priest pours water over the head above the baptismal font.

pg016_n0014: All peoples living in Kosovo have their own customs, which they have the right to practice.
pg016_n0015: Many customs are still practiced today, such as: the cutting of a child's hair for the first time by the godparent, abstaining from eating meat, or preparing a special dish on a certain day.
pg016_n0016: Norms and customs have been preserved from generation to generation.
pg016_n0017: Because of the development of human society, they have changed.
pg016_n0021: Social norm - a certain legal or moral rule for people's behavior in life or society.
pg016_n0022: Custom - a way of acting, behavior continuously repeated by someone, which is preserved for a long time.
pg016_n0023: Matchmaker - the arrangement of an engagement and marriage through a matchmaker/intermediary.

pg018_n0005: What do you know about property and inheritance?
pg018_n0007: Analyze the photograph and the given information.
pg018_im004: Grandfather and grandmother sitting next to each other on a bench in the park, holding each other with love and calmness.
pg018_n0014: Situation: Arta's grandfather and grandmother had worked hard throughout their lives.
pg018_n0015: They lived a simple life and saved money to secure material goods for themselves and their children.
pg018_n0016: They had a house and some property.
pg018_n0017: One day, they organized a family lunch with their children and discussed the inheritance.
pg018_n0018: They said: “All the wealth we have earned is shared.”
pg018_n0019: As we are growing old, we are happy to have you, our sons and daughters.
pg018_n0020: Therefore, this wealth, which we will divide equally among all of you, we want you to inherit.”
pg018_n0021: After grandfather finished, grandmother took the floor.
pg018_n0022: She explained that in the past, property was inherited only by the men and sons of the family.
pg018_n0023: Women and girls did not have the right to receive a share of their parents' property (or as it is known - hise).
pg018_n0024: A great injustice has been done to women and girls regarding inheritance.
pg018_n0025: - Today, all of us in the family are equal, so we are all heirs to the property, - said grandmother.
pg019_im004: Three question marks in green, blue, and orange.
pg019_n0008: How was the property divided in the past?
pg019_n0010: With the help of your parents or teacher, research on the internet and find information about the division of property in the past.
pg019_n0011: Compare it with today and see how women were discriminated against.
pg019_n0017: How were women and girls treated in the division of property?
pg019_n0019: Has the situation changed in our country?
pg019_n0021: Why were women and girls not part of the inheritance of property?
pg019_im005: An open book with a magnifying glass on top and sparkles around it.
pg019_n0026: The wealth that a person has created during his life is property.
pg019_n0027: It can be land, a dwelling, a business property, money, jewelry, a car, and other things.
pg019_n0028: Usually, property is inherited by family members.
pg019_n0029: The Constitution of Kosovo guarantees by law that both men and women have an equal right to inherit.
pg019_im003: An open book with numbers and mathematical symbols, decorated with small stars.
pg019_n0034: Share - the part that belongs to each person when a whole is divided.
pg020_n0005: Write how property used to be divided and how it is divided today.
pg020_n0009: Division of property in the past
pg020_sec001_ans_item-1: In the past, property was often divided unequally, usually giving more or only to boys, while girls were often excluded from inheritance.
pg020_sec001_ans_item-2: Today, property is divided equally among family members according to the law, regardless of gender; both girls and boys have the right to inherit.
pg020_n0017: Why is it important to have an equal right to inheritance among family members?

qz001_o0_exp: ❌ Not exactly. Borders show which neighboring states Kosovo borders, but not why its society is multiethnic.
qz001_o1_exp: ❌ No. Mountains are part of nature, but they do not show why a society is called multiethnic.
qz001_o2: 3) Because different peoples live in Kosovo
qz001_o2_exp: ✅ Correct! Kosovo is called multiethnic because different communities and peoples live there, with their own languages and traditions.
qz002_o0_exp: ❌ No. The text says that it is important to learn from others, but not to forget our culture and language.
qz002_o1: 2) Only people who travel for holidays
qz002_o1_exp: ❌ Not exactly. Going on holiday does not mean diaspora. Diaspora is connected with people who live outside their own country.
qz002_o2: 3) People who live far from their country
qz002_o2_exp: ✅ Correct! The diaspora is people who have left their country and live in other places, while preserving their origin and culture.
qz003_que: Today, who has the right to inherit equally?
qz003_o0_exp: ❌ Not correct. Parents may have property, but the inheritance belongs equally to the family's heirs.
qz003_o1_exp: ✅ Correct! Today, according to the law, both men and women have an equal right to inheritance.
qz003_o2_exp: ❌ Not correct. In the past, property was often given only to boys, but today this is not fair.

pg013_n0006_easy_read: Is the exchange of cultures among different peoples important?
pg013_n0011_easy_read:
People have left their country for different reasons.
Now they live in other countries of the world.
pg013_n0012_easy_read:
Diaspora means migrants or the children of migrants.
Their identity and cultural belonging have been shaped by their origin.
pg013_n0013_easy_read:
They learn from each other about:
- their language
- their culture
- their customs
So, they exchange cultures.
pg013_n0014_easy_read:
It is important to learn from others.
But we must not forget our own culture.
pg014_n0005_easy_read: Write what you have learned from your relatives who live in the diaspora.
pg014_n0010_easy_read: Write a message for your peers who live abroad.

- diaspora

pg015_n0006_easy_read: norm, custom, right, matchmaker, baptism, godfather, godmother.
pg015_n0011_easy_read: - How was society organized when there were no laws?
pg015_n0012_easy_read: Analyze the photographs with the given information.
pg015_n0017_easy_read: In the past there were no constitutions, laws, or parliaments.
pg015_n0018_easy_read: So that society and relations among people could function, people gathered and set rules for their behavior and relationships in the place where they lived.
pg015_n0020_easy_read:
Social norms are rules of behavior.
They have regulated relations among people.
They have resolved conflicts among them.
They have brought order to society.
pg015_n0021_easy_read:
Social norms were established by the people with more influence in society.
They did not seek the opinion of others.
Everyone had to follow these norms.
pg015_n0022_easy_read:
In the past, our people used the Kanun.
The Kanun is a body of unwritten customary norms.
These norms have been passed down from generation to generation.
pg015_n0023_easy_read:
In the past, disagreements were resolved according to the Kanun.
Today, laws determine how people should behave in society.
pg015_n0024_easy_read: Laws protect our rights and freedoms.
pg015_n0028_easy_read:
Customs are unwritten rules.
They vary according to different places and peoples.
pg015_n0029_easy_read: Customs are passed down from generation to generation.
pg015_n0030_easy_read:
Following customs is not mandatory.
But people are used to following them from time to time.
pg015_n0031_easy_read:
One of the customs is cutting a child's hair, which is called taking the shej.
This is done by a close member of the family, who is called the godfather.
pg015_n0035_easy_read:
Situation:
The grandparents were holding their wedding photograph in their hand.
They said that in their time marriages were arranged by matchmakers.
pg015_n0036_easy_read:
The parents proposed a girl for their son.
Then they chose a person who mediated between the boy's parents and the girl's parents.
This person was called the mediator or the matchmaker.
pg015_n0037_easy_read: This arranged marriage took place if the men of the family agreed to that marriage.
pg015_n0038_easy_read: When the men of the family agreed to the marriage of their children, they set the wedding date.
pg015_n0039_easy_read:
The bride's sending-off to the groom was done with a ceremony.
A traditional wedding was also organized.
pg015_n0040_easy_read: Today, marriages take place only with the mutual consent of the partners.
pg015_n0045_easy_read: The baptism of a child is an important event for every Catholic or Orthodox Christian family.
pg015_n0046_easy_read: Baptism has been practiced since ancient times.
pg015_n0047_easy_read: The parents made preparations for the day of the baptism.
pg015_n0048_easy_read:
The parents chose a believing couple: 
- the godfather
- the godmother
They are like second parents for the child.
In cooperation with the parents, they choose the child's name.
pg015_n0049_easy_read: The godfather and godmother usually give the child a coin or a gold ornament.
pg016_n0004_easy_read: How society was organized in the past.
pg016_n0005_easy_read:
Analyze it.
Then compare it with the way it is done today.
pg016_n0006_easy_read: Why is a child's baptism important?
pg016_n0014_easy_read:
All the peoples living in Kosovo have their own customs.
They have the right to practice these customs.
pg016_n0015_easy_read:
Many customs are still practiced today, such as:
- the child's hair being cut for the first time by the godparent
- not eating meat
- preparing a special dish on a certain day
pg016_n0016_easy_read: Norms and customs have been preserved from one generation to another.
pg016_n0017_easy_read: Because of the development of human society, norms and customs have changed.
pg016_n0021_easy_read:
A social norm is a certain rule.
This rule can be legal or moral.
It shows how people behave in life and in society.
pg016_n0022_easy_read:
A custom is a way of acting or behaving.
Someone repeats this behavior continuously.
This behavior is preserved for a long time.
pg016_n0023_easy_read: The matchmaker is the arrangement of engagement and marriage through an intermediary.
pg017_n0011_easy_read: Where were the norms of law written in the past?
pg017_n0015_easy_read:
Talk with your parents or grandparents.
Then write 1 custom.
This custom is observed according to the norms that were followed in their time.
pg018_n0005_easy_read: What do you know about property and inheritance?
pg018_n0007_easy_read:
Analyze the photograph.
Then analyze the given information.
pg018_n0012_easy_read:
These are the key words:
- property
- inheritance
- wealth
- equality
- injustice
pg018_n0014_easy_read:
Situation:
Arta's grandfather and grandmother had worked very hard throughout their lives.
pg018_n0015_easy_read:
They lived a simple life.
They saved money to provide material goods for themselves and for their children.
pg018_n0016_easy_read: They had 1 house and several properties.
pg018_n0017_easy_read:
One day, they organized a family lunch with their children.
They talked about inheritance.
pg018_n0018_easy_read: They said: “All the wealth we have earned is shared.”
pg018_n0019_easy_read:
We are growing old.
We are happy to have you, our sons and daughters.
pg018_n0020_easy_read:
Therefore, we want you to inherit this wealth.
We will divide it equally among all of you.”
pg018_n0021_easy_read: After grandfather finished, grandmother took the floor.
pg018_n0022_easy_read: She explained that in the past, wealth was inherited only by the men and boys of the family.
pg018_n0023_easy_read:
Women and girls did not have the right to receive a share of their parents' wealth.
This was also known as hise.
pg018_n0024_easy_read: A great injustice has been done to women and girls regarding inheritance.
pg018_n0025_easy_read:
Grandmother said:
“Today, everyone in the family is equal.
Therefore, we are all heirs to the wealth.”
pg019_n0008_easy_read: How was the wealth divided in the past?
pg019_n0010_easy_read:
With the help of your parents or your teacher, search on the internet.
Find information about the division of wealth in the past.
pg019_n0011_easy_read:
Compare the division of wealth in the past with the division of wealth today.
See how women have been discriminated against.
pg019_n0017_easy_read: How were women and girls treated when the wealth was divided?
pg019_n0019_easy_read: Has the situation changed in our country?
pg019_n0021_easy_read: Why were women and girls not part of the inheritance of wealth?
pg019_n0026_easy_read: Property is the wealth that a person has acquired during his life.
pg019_n0027_easy_read:
Property can be:
- land
- residential building
- business building
- money
- jewelry
- cars
- other things
pg019_n0028_easy_read: Usually, wealth passes as inheritance to family members.
pg019_n0029_easy_read: The Constitution of Kosovo guarantees by law that men and women have an equal right to inheritance.
pg019_n0034_easy_read: Hise is the part that belongs to each person when a whole is divided.
pg020_n0005_easy_read:
Write how wealth was divided in the past.
Also write how wealth is divided today.
